headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test for the first time on their soil
summary: The Tigers secure a dominant nine-wicket victory in Darwin, ending a 23-year wait for a Test win in Australia.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in a Test match in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz was a key figure in the triumph, claiming a decisive 5-66 in the second innings and scoring 65 runs in the first.
Hasan Mahmud set the tone early with a career-best 6-55 in the first innings, bowling Australia out for 198.
Bangladesh responded with a commanding 426 runs, led by Tanzid Hasan Tamim's first-ever Test century in Australia, along with strong contributions from Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque.
After securing a massive 228-run first-innings lead, the Tigers needed only 57 runs to win, which they achieved comfortably on the fourth morning.

Australian captain Pat Cummins admitted that Bangladesh 'outplayed us in all facets' of the match, while former cricketer Mark Waugh hailed it as one of the biggest upsets in Australian cricket history.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, describing the victory as one of the biggest in Bangladesh's cricket history across all formats.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz expressed his belief in the team's mindset and credited the overall team effort for the historic result.
caption:
A 23-year wait is over! Bangladesh just secured their first-ever Test victory on Australian soil.

Bangladesh achieved a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in a Test match in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz was a key figure in the triumph, claiming a decisive 5-66 in the second innings and scoring 65 runs in the first.

Hasan Mahmud set the tone early with a career-best 6-55 in the first innings, bowling Australia out for 198.

Bangladesh responded with a commanding 426 runs, led by Tanzid Hasan Tamim's first-ever Test century in Australia, along with strong contributions from Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque.

After securing a massive 228-run first-innings lead, the Tigers needed only 57 runs to win, which they achieved comfortably on the fourth morning.

Australian captain Pat Cummins admitted that Bangladesh 'outplayed us in all facets' of the match, while former cricketer Mark Waugh hailed it as one of the biggest upsets in Australian cricket history.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, describing the victory as one of the biggest in Bangladesh's cricket history across all formats.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz expressed his belief in the team's mindset and credited the overall team effort for the historic result.

headline: 20 of 30 accused absconding in Shapla Chattar case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has fixed September 3 as the next hearing date after prosecution reports that most of the warrants against the accused are unexecuted.
details: The prosecution informed the International Crimes Tribunal-2 that 20 of the 30 accused in the Shapla Chattar and Narayanganj crackdown cases have been confirmed as absconding.
The accused are facing charges of genocide and crimes against humanity related to the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists on May 5-6, 2013.
The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants for 30 fugitives, while 11 other accused individuals are already in custody.
During the latest hearing, nine of the detained accused were produced before the court, including former ministers Dipu Moni and Abdul Latif Siddiqui.
Two detained accused, former minister Hasanul Haq Inu and Abdur Razzaque, were not produced and the tribunal has ordered their appearance on September 3.
The court has also set September 3 for the submission of warrant execution reports for the remaining 10 accused individuals.
caption:
20 out of 30 accused in the Shapla Chattar crackdown cases are absconding.

The prosecution informed the International Crimes Tribunal-2 that 20 of the 30 accused in the Shapla Chattar and Narayanganj crackdown cases have been confirmed as absconding.

The accused are facing charges of genocide and crimes against humanity related to the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists on May 5-6, 2013.

The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants for 30 fugitives, while 11 other accused individuals are already in custody.

During the latest hearing, nine of the detained accused were produced before the court, including former ministers Dipu Moni and Abdul Latif Siddiqui.

Two detained accused, former minister Hasanul Haq Inu and Abdur Razzaque, were not produced and the tribunal has ordered their appearance on September 3.

The court has also set September 3 for the submission of warrant execution reports for the remaining 10 accused individuals.
